newsitem.title: HUNGARY: BORSODCHEM TO FOCUS ON PVC PROCESSING.
newsitem.headline: BORSODCHEM TO FOCUS ON PVC PROCESSING.

text.p: Hungarian chemicals company Borsodchem Rt said on Thursday it will sell minority stakes in two poliethylene processing plants while at the same time acquiring full ownership of a PVC processing plant.
"The portfolio change aims... a better focus on the fastest-growing PVC-processing sector of window frame extrusion," Borsodchem said in a statement.

The company said it plans to acquire a 50 percent stake in window-frame producer Panorama Kft from Austria's Actual Machinenbau AG, thus becoming the sole owner of Panorama, which has a 251.98 million forints share capital.
Borsodchem said it will sell its 25.34 percent stake, worth a nominal 74 million forints, in Marley-Gemenc Plast Rt to Marley European Holdings GmbH.
Borsodchem will also sell its 50.2 percent stake, worth a nominal 261 million forints, in Miskolci Muanyagfeldolgozo Rt to Netherland's Flair BV and Badine BV.
In a separate development, Borsodchem also announced it has signed a contract with Japan's Shin-Etsu Chemicals about a 40 thousand tonnes per year capacity increase of its Polimer II. plant.
The new capacity, planned to come on line in September 1998, will bring Borsodchem's total PVC capacity to 290,000 tonnes per year.
On the Budapest Stock Exchange Borsodchem shares closed at 6,520 forints, down 20.
